With online privacy being the number one technological concern in the world today what would be the best approach to being relatively off-the-grid while still using the Internet inside our homes? To someone who likes to surf the web and play pc games but concerned and quite frankly freaked the fuck out by the ever approaching big brother what advice would you give them regarding operating systems, game clients, Internet service providers, even cell phones? Questions regarding online privacy and anonymity.

First and foremost: avoid having all of your digital life in one place or through one provider. If you're even asking this question, I am already assuming you avoid the worst of the corporate surveillance tactics in Google products, Facebook, et al.

Realizing that none of this is a panacea towards combating government or corporate surveillance, here are a few pointers that I have collected over the past few months that will help increase your privacy and anonymity online. Research all third party products, and be wary even of some of the ones I have offered below. I would genuinely love to hear if there are better products or if my privacy assumptions need to be further questioned.

Use local file storage as much as possible, and avoid cloud services where feasible. Sync to your phone or USB keys manually.

Use DuckDuckGo for search.

Use Firefox as your web and mobile browser.

Look into Firefox extensions such as Adblock Edge and Ghostery. There are fantastic organizaitons like the Electronic Frontier Foundation that have endorsed various products such as Cookiemonster, BetterPrivacy, HTTPS Everywhere, NoScript, RefControl and Adblock Edge on the desktop. At a minimum be sure to block Facebook, Google+, Doubleclick and Google analytics cookies and scripts.

Use Telegram as a messenger client. Within Telegram, use the "Private Chat" feature when you can.

Use Signal (iOS) or TextSecure (Android) to encrypt your SMS messages. Ask your recipients to do the same.

Find an email provider or solution that allows for PGP encryption. It's OK to pay for email if you get a better product.

Do not store your passwords in the cloud.

Use iPredator's DNS.

Where possible, use a VPN.

Don't host pictures online.

If you use Android, CyanogenMod is a must.

Here's some suggestions and justifications - this is a more security approach:

Use Firefox because it's open source and developed by a not-for-profit (+ their new rendering engine's coming out soon!) and the extensions: 'NoScript' - NoScript allows you to prevent Javascript from executing on your browser at your discretion. Companies can, and will, identify you using your typing patterns along with mimetype enumeration + other things. The safest choice is to disable Javascript unless you absolutely need it.

PrivacyBadger - Like Ghostery, but produced by the Electronic Freedom Foundation (EFF), a reputable civil rights group that fights for the users in online privacy, I believe that that this is a better choice than Ghostery because Ghostery sells information to advertisers and has a commercial model. (http://www.businessinsider.com/evidon-sells-ghostery-data-to-advertisers-2013-6)

HTTPSEverywhere - Uses HTTPS as default on sites. Also developed by the EFF! Plugins and Mimetypes - If you need Javascript enabled, prevent enumeration of your plugins and mime settings. Can make fingerprinting harder.

Once you're done with those extensions, if you go to 'about:config', you can disable something called WebRTC that allows another layer of tracking to be applied by empowering website owners to get your real ip address if you're using a proxy (https://bloggeek.me/webrtc-new-york-times/) by visiting about:config in your browser, searching media.peerconnection.enabled and changing it to false. Make sure that you disable every plugin on your browser and don't enable Adobe Flash player as it will allow further fingerprinting of your browser. In settings > content > advanced, disable custom fonts! This is a security measure because font exploits can and will happen.

Use startpage.com as your search engine. This is they have received a bunch of awards and certifications (https://startpage.com/eng/protect-privacy.html)! Use private browsing at all times! This is because there is something called 'HTTPS Supercookies' can be used to track you between browser sessions, and private browsing will delete them on close. If you need cookies and you can't get stuffed adding an exception, enable them in the same settings window but set them to clear on close.

Now that that browser shizz is over...

Use a VPN! Use Google's DNS or your VPN's provider's DNS! Google will respect the law and they are very clear in how they use your access. Use a non-commercial operating system like a Linux distro, or, if you need to, use Mac OS X and disable all of the Spotlight information leakage that's enabled by default (Apple has nothing to gain financially by selling your information to advertisers)!

Use VMs (Virtual Machines) with Linux and a flashback set up if you have something to lose! (IE, need to visit Twitch? Launch VM with saved state > go to twitch inside VM > delete and rollback) I do this whenever I need to open stuff that I don't trust or if I need to use Flash. This is because they won't have access to your host computer, making it harder for them to identify you and your computer.

I'd use an iPhone. This is my personal opinion, this is because the hardware, software and services are developed by Apple, and software that is on the app marketplace is checked and signed by Apple to make sure that it's not loaded with any terms-of-use breaking nasties. This won't save you from the NSA however, because like any phone, the SIM card is running a tiny Java Virtual Machine and they are vulnerable to being broken into. Gov can also push updates to your phone through (over the air) OTA and it won't be pretty! Hell, if you can, don't use your phone with a cell network. Govs can downgrade cell version to get into your phone (I'll find example in a sec sorry). Also don't use email for jack shit! Use chatting services (Jabber) with OTR if you need to chat with someone about SJW infiltration tactics! Pidgin comes with OTR support preinstalled (I think?). Avoid email, and if you need to use it, use a commercial email provider because they won't try to make any dosh by selling info to advertisers (also read privacy agreements) or use that 'Tutanota'- but remember - trust needs to be earned.

These are just some suggestions. I'm sure that, combined with other people's suggestions (don't double dip on browser extensions tho), it'd be even better. PM me if you want any help with anything! I'll update this if other stuff springs to mind.
